title: Python String Methods and Text Validation
learningObjectives: Explain the core rules of python string methods and text validation in Python.
Write valid Python syntax for the operations covered in this topic.
Predict results for ordinary inputs and relevant edge cases.
Identify immutability, return values and error behaviour where applicable.
Apply the topic to a realistic text-processing task.

understand.concept: String methods provide reusable operations for searching, testing, trimming, splitting, joining and changing text. Most methods return a new value and leave the original string unchanged. Predicate methods such as isalpha() and isdigit() return Boolean results, while find() returns an index or -1.
understand.whyItMatters: String methods are building blocks for input validation, data cleaning, parsing simple records and searching text. Choosing the right method makes code clearer than manually scanning every character.
understand.analogy: String methods are like a text-processing toolkit: each tool performs one defined operation on a piece of text.
understand.analogyLimit: A method name does not guarantee full validation for a real-world format. For example, isdigit() does not validate an entire phone number, and split() is not a CSV parser.

explain.narrative:
## Searching and testing
`find(sub)` returns the first matching index or -1 if the substring is absent. `count(sub)` counts non-overlapping occurrences. `startswith()` and `endswith()` test prefixes and suffixes. Predicate methods such as `isalpha()`, `isdigit()`, `isalnum()` and `isspace()` return Boolean values; empty strings generally do not pass these character tests.

## Splitting and joining
`split(sep)` returns a list of parts. With no separator, runs of whitespace are treated as separators and leading/trailing whitespace is ignored. `separator.join(parts)` combines an iterable of strings. Every item supplied to join must be a string.

## Trimming and case handling
`strip()`, `lstrip()` and `rstrip()` remove whitespace from both, left or right edges. `lower()` and `casefold()` support normalized comparisons. These methods do not modify the original string. Do not use simple splitting as a replacement for a parser when the data format allows quoted delimiters or escaped fields.

practise.guidedTask: Create a short program that uses python string methods and text validation to process a realistic text value. Print each intermediate result and explain why it has that value.
practise.independentTask: Build a small text-processing utility using at least two operations from this lesson. Include a normal case, an empty or missing-value edge case, and a short explanation of the expected results.
hints: Start with a short, visible test string and write down its exact characters.
Check the return type of each operation before using the result.
Test both a typical input and a boundary or missing-value case.
Keep the original string in a separate variable when comparing transformed results.
Use repr() when whitespace or escape characters make output hard to inspect.
practise.challenge: Extend the utility to process a list of at least five text values. Explain one limitation of the chosen string operation and how you would handle it in a production application.

questions.prompt: What does find() return when the substring is absent?
questions.explanation: find uses -1 as the not-found result; index() instead raises ValueError.

questions.prompt: Which method tests whether all characters are digits?
questions.explanation: isdigit returns a Boolean based on whether all characters are digit characters and the string is non-empty.
split divides the string and returns a list of substrings.

questions.prompt: Which expression joins words with a hyphen?
questions.explanation: join is called on the separator string and consumes an iterable of strings.

questions.prompt: Why is split(',') not a complete CSV parser?
questions.answer: Quoted fields may contain commas and escaping rules
options: Quoted fields may contain commas and escaping rules
questions.explanation: CSV syntax includes quoting and escaping rules that a simple delimiter split does not implement.
